business_problem: Helvetia needed to simplify a cloud-native customer-data platform because DocumentDB and a separately synchronized Elasticsearch stack slowed feature delivery, complicated operations, and returned stale search results for teams that needed a real-time 360-degree view of customers and policies.
solution_summary: Helvetia replatformed its customer-data services from Amazon DocumentDB plus Elasticsearch to MongoDB Atlas and Atlas Search to support a cloud-native, event-driven sales platform on AWS. Apache Kafka streams changes from core insurance systems into team-owned data products, and Atlas stores the resulting JSON documents so front-end services can build a 360-degree view of customer and policy data. Atlas Search replaced a separately synchronized Elasticsearch estate, allowing Helvetia to deploy indexes through MongoDB APIs, keep database and search data automatically in sync, and query both through the same Java driver and query model. Because reindexing no longer requires Kafka sync changes, aliases, or manual cutovers, the platform can add features far faster while still returning millisecond search across tens of millions of documents. The simplified architecture reduces developer context switching and operational debugging across the company's expanding microservice portfolio.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Helvetia's cloud-native customer and policy data products for its sales and service microservices.

solution_components.name: Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Delivers integrated full-text and autocomplete search without a separate Elasticsearch synchronization layer.

data_flow: Core backend systems publish customer and policy changes through Apache Kafka, Atlas stores the resulting JSON data products, and Atlas Search indexes the same data automatically so front-end services can query a real-time 360-degree customer view through one MongoDB-based stack.
business_outcome: Helvetia cut release cycles from three to five days down to about three hours, accelerated feature rollouts by more than 90%, delivered search results in roughly 15 milliseconds across tens of millions of documents, and simplified development and operations across more than 30 Atlas-backed services.
